distinguishes: A nonce may be the chain's or one above a pending transaction's on every key it selects; a transaction sharing a key and a sequence with pending ones replaces them all, with a 10 percent bump over each, and evicts what then has a gap; four pending transactions a key and 64 an unstaked sender.

cases.name: a chain of three, then a gap and a stale nonce
cases.derivation: bob's sequence is 3 at the head; 0 is below it.

cases.name: a second key, and a transaction on both
cases.derivation: both: key 3 has k3 pending at 0, key 5 has k5 pending at 0; 1 is one above each. Re-read for 02-frame-pool.md version 8, whose FP-3 refuses key 0 beside another key, so the case uses keys 3 and 5 where it used 0 and 5.

cases.name: a replacement needs ten percent on both fees
cases.derivation: a-low raises max_fee by 10 percent but not the tip; a-high raises both.

cases.name: one replacement for two transactions that share its keys
cases.derivation: k12 has sequence 0 and shares key 1 with k1 and key 2 with k2: it replaces both.

cases.name: a replacement that drops a key evicts what then has a gap
cases.derivation: k1 replaces k13; key 3 then has no pending transaction at 0 and its chain sequence is 0, so k3 at 1 has a gap and is evicted.

cases.name: an eviction for space takes what it leaves with a gap
cases.derivation: With max_pending 2 the pool is full. FP-14's victim is the smallest (deadline, tip, -seq): a0, whose tip is 5. a1 at 1 then has no pending transaction at 0 on key 0, so it goes too (AM-10).

cases.name: four a key and no fifth
64 for an unstaked sender and no 65th
cases.derivation: 65 transactions on keys 1 to 65, each its own key; SAME_SENDER_MEMPOOL_COUNT is 64.

cases.name: no sender-wide limit for an active staked sender
cases.derivation: swallet is staked and has no reputation against it.
